title: HorizonLedger listing: scaling, KMS, and on-prem playback sync
summary: Redwood and HorizonLedger walked through the marketplace listing checklist, focused integration points for VPC and KMS, discussed on-prem playback connector performance and scaling, and agreed on a benchmark plan and security docs to share. Action items include a spike to run scale tests, KMS key rotation verification, and an updated ref-arch doc for listing submission.
action_items: Omar Singh: run 48-hr scale test using HL sample corpus and report latency/throughput - due 2027-05-06
Diego Morales: provide a sanitized 50GB sample workload and expected QPS profile - due 2027-04-27
Sophie Park: share HorizonLedger SOC2/KMS requirements matrix and any restrictive retention policies - due 2027-04-29
Priya Patel: update ref-arch diagram with on-prem connector flow + KMS sequence and upload to partner drive - due 2027-05-03
next_steps: Redwood to send the integration checklist and initial pricing assumptions by 2027-04-23
Schedule 1-hour lab session (scaling test) week of 2027-05-03
HorizonLedger to review and sign non-prod data share NDA by 2027-04-26
transcription:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neal (HorizonLedger CTO), Aisha Rahman (Eng PM), Diego Morales (Platform Eng), Sophie Park (Security)
Shared links: https://redwood.ai/partners/horizonledger/refarch-v1.pdf, https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/horizonledger-scale-template.xlsx

Summary (auto): quick sync on listing readiness and on-prem playback scaling. Lots of KMS questions and a request for a 48-hour stress run.

Topics: marketplace checklist, VPC/KMS, on-prem connector scaling, canary/fallback, benchmarks

Action items (captured): see metadata list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): ok hi everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through the listing checklist and then dive into the on-prem playback connector and the K-M-S integration points. quick intro round robin?
[00:18] Liam (HL - CTO): yeah hi Liam here, quick note, timeline is kinda tight for us, we want listing by mid-June for our GA push.
[00:27] Aisha (HL - Eng PM): and i'm Aisha, i'll own the PM side, sync with legal and infra for the onboarding.
[00:33] Omar (Redwood SE): Omar here, i'll lead the lab work and the scale tests, Priya is on the detailed diagrams after the call.
[00:40] Priya (Redwood SE): hi everyone, hi hi.
[00:45] Sophie (HL - Security): Sophie, security and compliance, i'll look at KMS/retention.

[02:05] Maya: ok first slide — listing readiness. we put together a small checklist on the drive, link in the notes. main items: ref-arch diagram, network connectivity (VPC peering or transit), KMS compatibility, telemetry/ops hooks, and a bench plan. any blockers on those from horizon side?
[02:28] Diego (HL - Platform Eng): network wise we prefer private link peering not open inbound. so need the marketplace connector to support VPC endpoints. also egress policies are strict.
[02:38] Omar: yeah that's fine — Redwood supports VPC ingress via our private connector; we have a set of templates for security groups and we can provide a sample terraform. small note: some places the doc says "private connector" but the runtime uses an envoy sidecar in the on-prem package, so that detail is in the ref-arch.
[03:05] Sophie: on KMS — we run a customer-managed KMS and require that keys are rotated every 90 days and that Redwood does not cache plaintext keys. is that supported?
[03:20] Priya: quick answer: yes, we support external KMS via our connector; we do not persist plaintext keys and we have an HSM integration option. the only caveat is when you enable cluster-autoscale there is a short period where the node might request a key (we use an ephemeral token).
[04:00] Liam: that ephemeral token bit — can you show the sequence? we need to show it to audits.
[04:08] Priya: i'll draw it out after this call and add it to the ref-arch, but high level: customer KMS -> signed token -> Redwood connector caches encrypted KV for X minutes -> runtime requests decrypted key via transient agent on node. i'll note though the transcript might say "K-V cash" cause speech to text hates it.
[05:15] Omar: yeah and to be explicit, when autoscale occurs we spin a new pod, it requests the key from the agent, agent requests from KMS, then we rotate short-lived credentials. we can instrument that in traces.

[07:00] Aisha: on the playback connector — that's the part that'll run in our on-prem datacenter and replay requests to the model for offline workloads. can it handle 2-3k QPS if we burst?
[07:14] Omar: ok we need to define burst pattern — sustained vs spikes. our default packing and batching targets for on-prem are tuned for low-latency small requests; for high throughput we recommend a dedicated pool and a continuous batching mode.
[07:45] Diego: our target is 2k sustained for 10 minutes and 5k bursts for up to 30s.
[08:00] Omar: got it. that's a realistic profile. two options: 1) dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) with explicit autoscale limits, or 2) hybrid mode where we route traffic through hosted fallback when on-prem is saturated. both have cost and latency tradeoffs.
[08:25] Liam: fallback to hosted — is data sent to hosted? we need data residency guarantees.
[08:33] Priya: we have a model variant routing policy: you can enable "no-hosted-fallback" so that requests that can't be served error instead of routing to hosted. or we can redaction/proxy — but that requires consent and would send only embeddings or anonymized payload. so it's a policy decision.
[09:00] Sophie: for compliance we prefer failing closed rather than routing data externally.
[09:06] Maya: noted — fail-closed is a supported config for the connector; we'll flag that in the checklist.

[11:20] Omar: on scaling tests — our recommended approach is a 48-hour run with ramp-up phases: 0-30m ramp to 2k QPS, hold 10 min, spike to 5k for 30s, then backdown; repeat patterns to exercise cache and K-V reuse. we need a sanitized dataset and exact QPS schedule. we also recommend toggling quantization and observing latency/regression.
[11:55] Diego: we'll produce a 50GB sample and the QPS spreadsheet, good.
[12:10] Aisha: also include the canary routing plan — we want to test canary on 5% traffic before full cutover. how does Redwood handle canaries?
[12:20] Omar: we support per-route percentages, header-based routing, and metric-based auto rollback if latency/error thresholds exceed X. you can also attach an SLO window. the console will show token-level cost and per-model latency.

[14:45] Liam: one more security ask — audit logs need to be immutable for 365 days, and we need a way to export to our SIEM (Splunk).
[14:58] Priya: Redwood can push audit logs to a customer-managed storage (S3 or on-prem syslog) and we have a Splunk HEC integration; retention policy is customer-controlled in the listing. i'll capture exact endpoints.

[17:30] Sophie: curious about KMS rotation during a canary. if a key rotates mid-canary, will messages in the KV cache fail?
[17:40] Omar: we handle key rotation by versioning the cache entries with key ID; on rotation, the runtime re-fetches and rewraps kv entries. but there's a small window where you might see transient decryption errors — we retry with exponential backoff and can fallback to re-requesting from KMS. we'll surface that in the canary SLO.

[20:05] Maya: i'd like to talk about the ref-arch doc — Priya, you mentioned you'd update the diag. can we include sequence diagrams for key rotation and for canary rollback?
[20:15] Priya: yes i'll add both sequences plus a network diagram showing private link and firewall rules. uploading to the partner drive after the call (link in notes).

[22:40] Diego: small nit — our infra uses a custom service mesh, will the Redwood connector's envoy sidecar conflict?
[22:50] Omar: we've seen this; we have a compatibility mode where the sidecar runs in host networking and we use IP-based rules. need to test in your lab.

[25:00] Aisha: what about telemetry — we need token-level cost attribution for cost forecasting. is that exposed?
[25:08] Maya: yes, console exposes token-level and route-level cost; for private deployments we can export telemetry to your monitoring stack and attach cost tags.

[27:30] Liam: back to the listing — what's the gating checklist from Redwood's side? is it just ref-arch and security docs?
[27:40] Maya: gate list: ref-arch diagram, connectivity checklist, KMS compatibility sign-off, bench run results, sample SLA for dedicated capacity (if used), and a partner listing metadata form. After those pass we do a final preflight UAT with your team.

[30:10] Diego: on the bench metrics — what latency percentiles do you target on-prem for 99p?
[30:17] Omar: depends on model size and quantization. our ballpark for 8-bit quantized medium models is 99p < 1.2s under 2k QPS with proper batching; for large models it's higher. the run will capture exact numbers.

[32:50] Sophie: any penalties or obligations if we request no-hosted-fallback? for instance does Redwood require a min committed capacity?
[33:00] Maya: for no-hosted-fallback with high availability needs we typically recommend dedicated capacity booking or a committed reserved pool. we can propose a pricing option in the follow-up.

[35:20] Aisha: ok let's confirm the lab schedule — Omar you said week of May 3rd?
[35:25] Omar: yes week of May 3rd, I'll create a calendar invite and include the runbook.

[37:10] Priya: also we'll provide a short preconfigured Helm chart and a sample terraform module for VPC peering in the partner repo.

[39:40] Diego: one more thing — we use key rotation every 90 days. can Redwood accept a rotate-without-rolling policy or do we need to drain nodes?
[39:55] Omar: rotate-without-rolling is doable because we use short-lived node creds; however if you rotate and want to invalidate caches immediately we recommend a controlled rolling to avoid transient errors. we'll document the two options.

[41:30] Liam: are there any known issues with quantized models + our custom mesh?
[41:38] Omar: mostly around custom jitter in the mesh causing increased tail latency; quantization itself is fine. recommend we run a mesh-aware test in the lab.

[43:00] Maya: recap: Redwood will send the integration checklist & pricing by tomorrow; Priya will update the ref-arch with sequences; Omar will run the 48-hour scale once Diego provides the sample; Sophie to send KMS matrix. we'll schedule the lab week of May 3rd.
[43:30] Aisha: thanks everyone this was good.
[43:36] Sophie: thanks.
[43:40] Liam: thanks, appreciate it.

[45:00] Meeting end.
